result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_min_eccentricity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get minimum eccentricity (graph radius). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L28595-L28647){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_min_eccentricity(unconnected=True) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Minimum eccentricity](/assets/graphs/get-min-eccentricity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node graph with each node's eccentricity in a badge: A 4, B 3, C 2, D 2, E 3, F 4. The middle nodes C and D have the smallest value and are drawn in the accent color; the card gives the minimum eccentricity 2." width="100%"} Alias for `get_radius()`. The minimum eccentricity is the smallest maximum distance from any node to all other nodes. A node's eccentricity is the number of hops to the farthest node it can reach; the node(s) with the smallest eccentricity form the *center* of the graph and are the best starting points when the worst-case distance to everyone else matters. Distances are counted in hops (edge weights are ignored) and, in directed graphs, follow edge directions. Nodes that reach nothing (isolated nodes, or nodes without outgoing edges in a directed graph) have eccentricity `0`, which makes the result `0` under the default `unconnected=True`. See `get_radius()` for details. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [unconnected]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Controls what happens when some nodes cannot reach each other. If `True` (default), each node's eccentricity only considers the nodes it can reach and the smallest one is returned, pooled across all components. If `False`, returns `None` for a graph that is not connected (weak connectivity for directed graphs). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum eccentricity (radius), or `None` if disconnected (when `unconnected=False`). Also `None` for an empty graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a star graph the center reaches every other node in one step, so the minimum eccentricity is `1`: ::: {#824e0009 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5) graph.get_min_eccentricity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: In a path of six nodes the two middle nodes are each at most three hops from either end, so the minimum eccentricity is `3`; the result always matches `get_radius()`: ::: {#54da8ff4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(6) (path.get_min_eccentricity(), path.get_radius()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 3) ``` ::: :::
